title: Optimize walkthrough: quant profiles INT8/FP8 - Apollo Analytics
summary: Redwood Optimize walkthrough focused on INT8 vs FP8 quantization profiles, quality vs latency tradeoffs for Apollo's multi-turn summarization pipelines. Discussed baseline hosted latency/cost, Dedicated options, runbook for pilot benchmarks and next steps to share quantization benchmarks and security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we scheduled 55 minutes, we'll walk through Redwood Optimize quant profiles for INT8 and FP8, and show quality vs latency plots. Samira from SE will run the demo.
[00:18] Jordan (Apollo): Thanks, we have Priya and Marcus on the call. high level: our use case is multi-turn customer support summarization, strict 200ms p95 target for short updates, and longer batch summary jobs ok to be higher.
[00:35] Samira (SE): got it, that's helpful. quick qual — are you on hosted today or running any self-hosted endpoints?
[00:42] Priya: currently hosted with another vendor, we do run some on-prem for PII workloads but most is in cloud; curious about dedicated capacity and the per-token economics.
[00:52] Alex: perfect, we'll cover both. deck link: https://redwood.internal/decks/optimize-quant-profiles (shared).
[01:10] Samira: okay jumping into the slides — first slide shows baseline fp16 quality and latency for the model you mentioned in the intake form, a 13B LLM. FP8 and INT8 numbers discussed are relative to that. note: some transcription nukes model names as Red wood Optima, ignore that.
[02:05] Jordan: can you give us the expected quality drop for int8 for summarization? our evals are pretty sensitive to hallucination.
[02:14] Samira: yes so from our benchmarks on similar summarization prompts we see INT8 gives ~1-3% BLEU/ROUGE-ish drop for 13B models depending on prompt distribution, but latency improvement is substantial — about 25-35% drop in tokens/sec latency p95 on the same GPU. FP8 often sits between FP16 and INT8 on latency but with smaller quality loss ~0.5-1.5%.
[02:45] Priya: 1-3% could be material. is that stable across prefixes and long contexts?
[02:53] Samira: it varies. prefix caching and kv cache behavior matter — for long contexts INT8 quant noise can accumulate and we recommend either KV-cache warming or using mixed precision (FP8 for attention layers, INT8 for FFN). that's what our quant profiles do.
[03:20] Marcus: what about throughput for batch summarization — we run nightly batches of 100k docs, cost is a big driver.
[03:28] Alex: for batch workloads INT8 typically reduces cost per token by 30-45% depending on hardware and batching. we recommend dedicated pools for predictable throughput; you can pick autoscale to run spot/burst for off-peak.
[03:45] Samira: demo time — I'll switch to the console. (screen share) starting Redwood Console -> Optimize -> Quant Profiles. you can see preset profiles: conservative-fp8, balanced-int8, throughput-int8-max, mixed-fp8-int8.
[04:15] [screen noise / faint crosstalk]
[04:30] Samira: selecting balanced-int8 — note the profile toggles: per-layer override, per-op clamp thresholds, and fallback to fp16 for specific ops. you can also run a quality evaluation by uploading a prompt set; I'm going to run a quick micro-eval against your sample prompts (we loaded the small sample you sent).
[05:05] Jordan: that's cool, will the micro-eval use the same metric set we use? we use ROUGE-1/2 and an internal hallucination score.
[05:14] Samira: yes you can configure metrics; we have a custom metric plugin so you can plug in your hallucination heuristics; we'll run the default quick eval then schedule the full eval. starting eval...
[06:00] [pause / typing]
[06:12] Samira: results coming in — baseline fp16 quality = 0.82 (our normalized score), balanced-int8 = 0.79, fp8-conservative = 0.81. latency p95 per request: fp16 = 320ms, balanced-int8 = 220ms, fp8-conservative = 260ms on an A100-80GB equivalent.
[06:44] Priya: ok numbers look promising. what's the variance across longer conversations?
[06:50] Samira: for multi-turn sessions we measure latency per-token; p95 for long sessions in balanced-int8 was 18% lower vs fp16, but quality drift was more noticeable on hallucination-sensitive prompts. we can run a targeted eval on your multi-turn dataset.
[07:20] Jordan: can we do a canary rollout that starts in fp16 then flips to int8 for X% of traffic?
[07:28] Alex: yes — Redwood supports rollout policies: canary by percentage, per-route, or by latency bucket. automatic rollback on quality regression is available if you wire the eval hooks.
[07:44] Tina (SRE): questions on determinism and reproducibility — quantization is tricky for debugging. how do we trace a misbehaving request back to the model profile?
[07:55] Samira: good Q — every request carries model_version, quant_profile, and kernel metadata in the trace. Console has a trace viewer and we persist call-level inputs/outputs per your retention policy (we can disable storing user text for PII).
[08:15] Marcus: security/compliance — do you support SSO/SAML and customer-managed KMS?
[08:22] Alex: yes to both. we have SOC2 Type II, ISO docs and we'll share a security packet. for Private we support VPC peering and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS/HSM.
[08:38] Priya: what's the impact of quantization on embedding quality? we also embed the summaries for search.
[08:45] Samira: embedding nets are less tolerant; INT8 generally not recommended for embeddings if you need high-precision distances. FP8 or FP16 recommended. our Optimize will suggest per-route profiles — e.g., generate-summary route -> balanced-int8, embed-route -> fp16/fp8.
[09:10] [10 mins jump in timestamps — condensed]
[19:30] Samira: returning to the evaluation page — I launched a full run for your larger prompt set; expected finish ~2 hours. I added your hallucination metric and ROUGE. we'll email results.
[19:48] Jordan: for pilot, what infra do we need? can we trial on hosted or do we need Dedicated?
[19:56] Alex: you can do a hosted pilot; if you need network isolation we can do Private or Dedicated. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput for nightly batches. Pilot typically runs 2-4 weeks for realistic load and evaluation.
[20:15] Priya: curious about hardware: does FP8 rely on specific GPU support? we use mixture of cloud SKUs.
[20:22] Samira: FP8 benefits from newer hardware with tensor core support; however our runtime has kernels that emulate fp8 on older GPUs with some perf penalty. we'll include a hardware compatibility matrix in the follow-up.
[20:40] Marcus: any red flags using int8 for classification or reranking?
[20:47] Samira: for reranking you often need more numeric stability — we usually recommend fp8 or fp16. INT8 can be okay if you have large margin between items, but it's riskier.
[21:10] Jordan: competitors — have you compared to vendor X?
[21:15] Alex: we run internal comparisons vs Anthropic, OpenAI, Mosaic (mentioned) for perf/cost; results vary by model and workload. we'll share anonymized benchmark sheets.
[21:30] [noise / someone joins late]
[22:00] Samira: now demoing the quality vs latency chart: on the console there's an interactive plot where X axis = latency p95 and Y axis = normalized quality score. you can hover to see profile details. (shows clustered points: fp16 higher quality/higher latency, fp8 in middle, int8 lower latency lower quality).
[22:40] Priya: can we set a hard constraint like "latency < 250ms p95" and get recommended profiles?
[22:47] Samira: yes that's a new Optimize feature — constraint-driven recommendations. you input target latency and quality tolerance and Optimize outputs a ranked set of profiles and expected cost delta.
[23:10] Jordan: for our nightly batch we care more about cost and throughput; for live chat we care about p95. can we have per-route profiles?
[23:18] Samira: absolutely, per-route and per-model policies. you can pin a model+profile per route.
[23:35] Alex: touching on rollout — you can schedule gradual rollouts with auto-eval gating; if the quality drops beyond threshold it will rollback and alert.
[23:48] Tina: what's observable in logs vs Console? our SRE prefers Prometheus metrics.
[23:55] Samira: we emit Prometheus metrics for latency, token counts, quantized kernel counters, and have a tracing exporter for Jaeger/OTel. logs include model_version and quant_profile labels.
[24:20] [mid-call recap by Alex]
[24:30] Alex: quick recap: INT8 = best cost/throughput, moderate quality risk; FP8 = good middle ground; use mixed profiles for sensitive workloads. next steps: run full eval on your dataset, schedule a benchmark on your infra, share security packet and pricing.
[24:50] Jordan: agreed. can you include estimated cost savings for our 100k nightly batch?
[24:58] Alex: yes, we'll prepare a cost model - need a few inputs (token counts, avg length). Priya already shared some numbers, we'll fill the rest.
[25:10] Samira: creating next steps in console — sending invite for a 2-week pilot kickoff and adding the pilot checklist.
[25:25] [action item notes typed]
[26:00] Marcus: any gotchas we should know before pilot?
[26:06] Samira: watch out for distribution shift — synthetic quick evals can overestimate quality. always run on production-ish data. and make sure to pin stable kernels for reproducibility.
[26:25] Priya: timeline — we can start pilot next week if we lock down config.
[26:31] Alex: I'll loop in AE and Solutions to get contract details.
[26:40] [wrap-up]
[26:45] Alex: alright thanks everyone. we'll send the security pack, quant benchmark sheet, and a proposed pilot SOW. any final Qs?
[26:52] Jordan: none from me. thanks.
[27:00] [call ends — note: actual call ~55 minutes, transcript condensed for key segments, full logs saved in Console.]
